parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *akja (“edge”), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *agjō. The semantic shift likely occurred via a derived adjective aajaton (“boundless”) (still found in dialects), originally literally “edgeless”; after the original word was forgotten, aaja (“broad, vast”) was then derived as a back-fo
From Proto-Finnic *ahjo (compare Estonian ahi), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *asjǭ (whence Swedish ässja).

parole.significato: abandoned swidden; a grassy open or cleared space in a (former) forest cleared by slash-and-burn cultivation, but, due…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *aho, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *askǭ (compare English ashes and Swedish aska).

parole.significato: time (inevitable progression into the future with the passing of present and past events)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *aika, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).

From Proto-Finnic *ainaga (compare Estonian ainus, Ingrian ainava, Livonian āinagi, Ludian ainag, Votic ainõgo), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *ainagaz (“sole”) (from *ainaz (“one”), compare Latin unicus (“unique”)).

parole.significato: oar (implement used to row a boat)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *airo (compare Estonian aer), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *airō (“oar”) (compare Swedish åra). First attested in 1452 (in the place name Ayrosalmj, modern Airosalmi).
From Proto-Finnic *airu-, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *airuz. The -t in the singular forms is likely analogous.

parole.significato: husk (of a grain); (in the plural) chaff (inedible parts of a plant whose seeds are eaten as grain)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *akana (compare Estonian agan, Livonian agānd, Votic akanõ), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *aganō (“chaff”) (compare Swedish agn). Attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552).

parole.significato: a closed body of water, e.g. a lagoon
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *aldas (compare Karelian allaš (“trough”)), derived from a root borrowed from Proto-Germanic *aldǭ (“trough”) (whence e.g. Norwegian olda and separately also aalto). The ending has probably been modified to -as by analogy with other Germanic loans (such as valas).
From Proto-Finnic *ani (compare Karelian ani, Veps ani), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *an + -i.

parole.significato: to earn, make, win, gain (e.g. money)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic [Term?] (compare Karelian ašnita); originally *asnaita, asnata (attested in 1787). The modern form is probably by folk etymology with ansa (“trap”) (and to avoid the hard-to-pronounce -sn-; compare känsä from earlier käsnä). The Finnic word is probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic

parole.significato: truss (structure made up of one or more triangular units made from straight beams of wood or metal, which is used to su…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ansas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *ansaz.

parole.significato: sole, outsole (of a foot or shoe)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *antura, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *anduraz. Cognate with Ingrian antura, Estonian andur (“keel”), Old Norse ǫndurr (“snowshoe”) and Swedish andor.
From Proto-Finnic *apara, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Norse afr).
From Proto-Finnic *arka (compare Estonian arg), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *argaz (compare Old Norse argr).

parole.significato: everyday life, daily life, normal life (ordinary, mundane or non-special days in life)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *arki, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *argį̄ (“wickedness”).
From Proto-Finnic *armas (compare Estonian armas, Veps armaz), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *armaz (“pitiful, pitiable”).

parole.significato: lot (anything, as a die, pebble, ball, or slip of paper, used in determining a question by chance)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *arpa (compare Ingrian arpa), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *arbaz (whence Old Norse arfr, Swedish arv).
From Proto-Finnic *arpi (compare Livonian ärb), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *arwaz, *arwiz (“scar”).
] From Proto-Finnic *atra (compare Estonian ader), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *arþrą (compare Old Norse arðr), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂érh₃trom.
From Proto-Finnic *autijo, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *auþijaz.
From Proto-Finnic *autugas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *audagaz. Compare Gothic 𐌰𐌿𐌳𐌰𐌲𐍃 (audags, “blessed”).
From Proto-Finnic *auvo, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *aują (compare Proto-Norse ᚨᚢᛃᚨ (auja), Old Norse ey (“luck, heavenly aid”)). Cognate with Estonian au, Karelian auvo and Livonian o’v.

parole.significato: to fly (to move in air or quickly)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *entädäk, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Norse inna).
From Proto-Finnic *ettoneh, somehow derived from Proto-Germanic *etaną.

parole.significato: trammel hook (kitchen utensil used to hang a pot over an open fire hearth and to regulate its height over the fire)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hahila (compare Estonian ahel, Ingrian hahlat, Karelian hoahla, Ludian huahlad, Veps hahl and Votic ahilõ), borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old High German hāhala, hāhal, Luxembourgish Héil, Alemannic German Hääli).

parole.significato: heron (any wading bird of the Ardeidae family in order Pelecaniformes)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *haikara (variant of *haikari), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *haigrô (compare English heron).

parole.significato: A single, usually thin hair or fiber.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *haiva-, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hawją (“hay”) (whence e.g. Swedish hö, English hay); modern form and meaning via contamination by haven (“hair”).
From Proto-Finnic *haja- (compare Estonian hajuma, Veps hajeta), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sājan-, *sēaną (compare Gothic 𐍃𐌰𐌹𐌰𐌽 (saian), Swedish så).

parole.significato: to hit something repeatedly (as a nail with a hammer or a log with an axe)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hak'at'ak (compare Estonian hakkama, Livonian akkõ, Votic akatõ). Further origin is disputed, with possible links to Uralic (compare Moksha [script needed] (tšakams), Udmurt шуккыны (šukkyny)) and Germanic (compare Swedish hacka, English hack, from Proto-Germanic *hakkōną) words.

parole.significato: to (go) get, fetch, retrieve, (find and) bring
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hakëdak, borrowed from early Proto-Germanic *sākija- (later *sōkijaną, compare English seek).
From Proto-Finnic *halait'ak, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *halōną, *halōjaną.

parole.significato: to rule, govern, reign, administer, command
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *haldit'ak, the root borrowed from Proto-Germanic *haldaną and derived with + -ita.
From Proto-Finnic *hamëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hamiz (compare Old Norse hamr) or *hamô (“shirt”) (compare Old English hama).
From Proto-Finnic *hardas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *harduz.
From Proto-Finnic *habukka, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *habukaz.
From Proto-Finnic *hauta (compare Estonian haud), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sauþaz (compare Old English sēaþ).

parole.significato: to observe, detect, perceive, find, spot, notice
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *havait'ak (compare Ingrian havaita, Karelian havaittšuo, Ludian havaitšuda, Votic havattsaassõ); the root is a borrowing from Proto-Germanic *hawāną (“to observe”) + -ita.
Compound of heisi (“string, thread”, dialectal) + mato (“worm”), the initial component from Proto-Finnic *häici (“string, thread”), which is borrowed from Proto-Germanic *saidô.

From Proto-Finnic *heittädäk (compare Estonian heitma, Livonian eitõ, Veps heitta), possibly from earlier *šej-ttä- and borrowed from Early Proto-Germanic *sēja-/*sēje- (later Proto-Germanic *sēaną; compare Swedish så (“to sow (seeds)”)).
From Proto-Finnic *hëlppo (compare Estonian hõlp, Ingrian helppo, Karelian helppo), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *helpō (compare English help and Swedish hjälp).

parole.significato: slow (at a low speed; not fast, not quick)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hidas (compare Karelian hijaš), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sīþaz (compare German seit).

parole.significato: silt, fine sand (technical definition: mineral soil with dominating particle size from 20 μm to 60 μm)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hëëta, from earlier *šeeta, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sēda-, *sēdiz.
From Proto-Finnic *hilja, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *silāną.
From Proto-Finnic *hipjä, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hiwją. Cognate to English hue.
From Proto-Finnic *hiuka (“hunger, starvation”) (compare Ingrian hiuvata, Karelian hiuvata, Votic iukaa (“to torment”)), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sūganą.

parole.significato: mold, mildew (furry or woolly growth of tiny fungi)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *homëh (compare Karelian homeh, Votic õmõ), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *swammaz.
From Proto-Finnic *hopëda (compare Estonian hõbe), from earlier *šopeta, originally meaning "soft", possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *samftijaz (“soft”).

parole.significato: very large; immense, enormous, huge, whopping, incomparable
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *huikëda, the root of which is possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *swiką. Related to Karelian huikie (“shameful”) and Veps huiged (“indecent, shameful”).

parole.significato: grain that is rejected in threshing due to lightness of seeds
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Finnic *hulëh, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hul- (compare English hull).
From Proto-Finnic *hookjas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hōgjaz. Compare huojentaa, huojentua.
From Proto-Finnic *hootra, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *fōdrą.

parole.significato: to back water, back the oars
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hoobat'ak, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?].
From Proto-Finnic *hurskas (compare Karelian hurskas (“brisk, quick”)), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hurskaz.

From Proto-Finnic *hüp'äit'äk, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *huppōną, *huppijaną (“to move up and down; hop”), compare German hüpfen (“to hop”). Compare also Erzya чопавтомс (čopavtoms, “to dive”).
From Proto-Finnic *häirit'äk, from earlier *šajri-/*šäjri-, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sairijaną (compare Icelandic særa).

parole.significato: shame (uncomfortable or painful feeling; something to regret; reproach incurred or suffered; dishonour; ignominy; deris…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *häpedä (compare Estonian häbe, Votic äppiä), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hawiþą (compare Old Norse háð (“mockery”)).
From Proto-Finnic *hätä (compare Estonian häda, Ludian hädä, Veps häda), borrowed from early Proto-Germanic *sētā (later *sētō, compare Swedish såt, försåt (“ambush”), Old English sǣt (“ambush”)).

parole.significato: fat (adipose tissue of an animal, especially of a pig)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *icra (compare Karelian isra, Veps izr), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *instraz (compare Icelandic ístra, Swedish ister).
From Proto-Finnic *ilkëda, probably borrowed (and derived) from Proto-Germanic *ilhilaz (“bad, evil”). Cognates include Karelian ilkie, Estonian ilge, English ill.

From Proto-Finnic *ja (compare Estonian ja, Ingrian ja, Livonian ja, Votic ja), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *jahw (“and”) (compare Gothic 𐌾𐌰𐌷 (jah), Old High German ja, joh). Attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552).

parole.significato: party, celebration, carnival, fiesta, jubilee (social gathering of usually invited guests for entertainment, fun and so…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *juhla (compare dialectal Estonian juhlad), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *jehwlą. Doublet of joulu.

parole.significato: to scrape (to remove, dislodge, clean, empty with a scraping movement or action)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaap(p)idak (compare Estonian kaapima, Karelian koapie, Livonian kōpšõ, Ludian kuabita, Veps kabita), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skabaną (“to scrape”).

parole.significato: decoy (for hunting, especially for birds where the decoy is an image of a bird)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaavëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skawwiz.
From Proto-Finnic *kadëh (compare Estonian kade, Karelian kajeh, Livonian ka’d, Veps kadeh, Võro kadõ), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skaþiz (compare Gothic 𐍃𐌺𐌰𐌸𐌹𐍃 (skaþis)).

parole.significato: a type of traditional trap for catching birds, especially black grouse
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaha, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kazą.

parole.significato: railing, rail (fence or barrier consisting of one or more horizontal rails and vertical supports)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaidëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skaidiz (compare Old Norse skeiðir). The weaving sense “reed” appears to have been the original one.

parole.significato: rush, bulrush, club-rush (grass-like plants of the genus Scirpus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaisla (*kaisila), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gaisilaz (“staff, whip”) (compare German Geißel and Swedish gissel).
From Proto-Finnic *kaita (compare Ingrian kaita, Karelian kaita, Livvi kaidu, Ludian kaid, Veps kaid), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gaidō (compare English goad).

parole.significato: to long for, yearn for, pine for, miss
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaibait'ak (compare Estonian kaebama, Karelian kaivata, Livonian kaibõ, Võro kaibama), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kawjaną, which is ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *gewH- (“to call, cry out”).
From Proto-Finnic *kalëh (“husk; chaff”), probably borrowed and derived from Proto-Germanic *skalō.

parole.significato: synonym of äyräs (“bank (of a river, etc.)”)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaldas (compare Estonian kallas), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *halþaz (compare Old Norse hallr).

parole.significato: rock (the aggregate of solid mineral matter (stone) that constitutes a significant part of the earth's crust)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kallijo (compare Estonian kalju, Ingrian kallio, Karelian kallivo, Veps kal, Votic kalʹlʹo), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hallijǭ.
From Proto-Finnic *kalvadak, borrowed by metathesis from Proto-Germanic *klawjaną.

parole.significato: chicken (domestic fowl of species Gallus gallus, Gallus domesticus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kana (compare Estonian kana), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hanô (“rooster, cock”) (compare German Hahn).

From Proto-Finnic *kangas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gangaz (compare Danish gang (“forty warp threads”), Middle High German ganc (“warp count (in weaving)”), Middle Low German ganc (“warp count (in weaving)”)).

parole.significato: A soil type: firm, moraine ground covered with a relatively thin layer of organic topsoil called podsol.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kangas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gangaz (“way, passage”) (compare German Gang), boreal forests being easily passable.

parole.significato: people, nation (community of people united by shared culture or ethnicity, or the inhabitants of a country)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kansa (compare Livvi kanzu, Veps kanz), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hansō (earlier *hansā, compare Gothic 𐌷𐌰𐌽𐍃𐌰 (hansa)).

parole.significato: trousseaux (clothes, linen etc. collected or brought by the bride to their new home after being married)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kapijot, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (whence dialectal Swedish gävo), from Proto-Germanic *gebaną.

parole.significato: a unit of measure for the volume of dry goods, equivalent to 1/32 of a tynnyri or 4.58 litres in the Kingdom of Sweden…
parole.testo: [Alt: A cubical wooden measuring vessel, a kappa.] From Proto-Finnic *kappa (compare Estonian kapp, Ingrian kappa, Karelian kappa, Kukkuzi kappa, Ludian kappe), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skapaz (compare Old Saxon skap (“a measure”), Old High German scaf (“vessel”)).

parole.significato: cattle (domesticated bovine animals) (sometimes with a specifier: nautakarja, lehmikarja)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karja (compare Estonian kari, Livonian kōŗa), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *harjaz (“army”) (compare Swedish här (“land army”), German Heer (“army”)). The original sense "army, forces" may survive in Karjala.
From Proto-Finnic *kartano (compare Karelian kartano, Livonian kǭrand (with metathesis), Votic kartõno), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gardô (“enclosure, yard, garden”).

From Proto-Finnic *karvas (compare Livonian kǭraz), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *harwaz (compare Middle High German hare, German herb) or (less likely) derived from Proto-Uralic *karwa (compare Udmurt курыт (kuryt), Komi-Permyak курыт (kuryt), Komi-Zyrian курыд (kuryd), Eastern Khanty корә
From Proto-Finnic *katras, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gaduraz (whence Old English geador); no other Finnic cognates are known.

parole.significato: pot, cooking pot, stockpot, saucepot, kettle (often cylindrical or nearly cylindrical cooking vessel for fast cooking o…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kattila, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *katilaz.

parole.significato: shade, shadow (relative darkness caused by the interruption of light)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *katvëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skaduz ~ *skadwaz (compare English shade, shadow). No cognates in the other Finnic languages are known.
From the stem *kauka, from Proto-Finnic *kauka-, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hauhaz, from Proto-Indo-European *kewk-. Cognate to Estonian kauge and Votic kauga.
From Proto-Finnic *kaunis (compare Estonian kaunis), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skauniz (compare English sheen, German schön, Swedish skön).

From Proto-Finnic *kakra (compare Estonian kaer, North Karelian kakra, Livonian ka’ggõrz), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hagrō (compare Old Swedish haghre, dialectal Swedish hagre, Old Gutnish hagri).

parole.significato: deer (any relatively small deer of unspecified species, especially roe deer) (not as a zoological term)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kapris, borrowing from Proto-Germanic *habraz, *hafraz (“he-goat”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kápros. Cognates include Estonian kaber, Karelian kabris.
From Proto-Finnic *kauto, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skautaz.

parole.significato: a creature related to the moon, sky or air
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kabëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skapiz (compare Proto-Germanic *skapą, Old English gesceap). Cognate with Estonian kabu, Karelian kaveh, Võro kabo and Proto-Samic *kuopës (“witch”).

parole.significato: hoof (thick keratin covering of the tip of a toe of an ungulate)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kapja + -o (compare dialectal kapia, Estonian kabi, Votic kabjõ), ultimately perhaps borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hāfaz.

parole.significato: spear (long stick with a sharp tip used as a weapon for throwing or thrusting)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaihas (compare Ingrian keihäs, Veps keihaz), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gaizaz (compare Old Norse geirr, German Ger). Doublet of kaira.
From Proto-Finnic *keldeh, probably ultimately borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skelduz, or less likely from Baltic (compare Lithuanian ski̇̀ltis).

From Proto-Finnic *kello (compare Karelian kello, Ludian kello, Veps kelo), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skellǭ (“bell”) (compare German Schelle and Swedish skälla (“bell”)). The original sense is “bell”; the second sense “clock” developed from the fact that time was traditionally marked by church
From Proto-Finnic *këno (compare Estonian kenus), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kenwuz (later *kinnuz), albeit the semantic development would not be entirely clear.

parole.significato: to shear (remove the fleece from a sheep)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kerit'äk, derived from a root borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skeraną, as ker- + -itä.
From Proto-Finnic *kërnas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gernaz (“eager, willing”).

parole.significato: a traditional measure for sold lampreys, consisting of 31 lampreys (30 in a bunch tied and held together with one more)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kërpo, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kerbą (whence Old Norse kerfi (“bundle”), Swedish kärve).

From Proto-Finnic *kërsa (compare Võro kõrźo), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Norse kjarr (“copsewood”)). The meaning "kid, child, brat" would in this case be a re-extraction from kersalapsi (“bastard, illegitimate child”, literally “a child conceived/born in the bushes”)
From Proto-Finnic *kihla, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gīslaz (“hostage”).
From Proto-Finnic *kilpi (compare Estonian kilp, Livonian kiļb, more distantly also Northern Sami galba), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hlībō (compare Old Norse hlíf).
From Proto-Finnic *kippo, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kippǭ.

parole.significato: to scream, shriek, cry out (let out a high-pitched scream)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kirkudak, possibly borrowed by metathesis from Proto-Germanic *skrīkijaną, if not onomatopoeic.
From Proto-Finnic *kiusat'ak (compare Estonian kiusama, Karelian kiusata, Livonian kiužõ, Votic čiuzõtõ), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *keusaną (compare Gothic 𐌺𐌹𐌿𐍃𐌰𐌽 (kiusan, “to test, to prove”)).
From Proto-Finnic *kolëda, probably a nativized borrowing from Proto-Germanic *kōluz.
From Proto-Finnic *kotti, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kuddô.
From Proto-Finnic *kuha (compare Estonian koha, Veps kuha, Votic kuha), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *guzaz (compare Swedish gös).
From Proto-Finnic *kuhilas, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skūilaz.

parole.significato: purse, coin purse (small bag for carrying money)
parole.testo: According to one theory, from Proto-Finnic *kukkaro (compare Estonian kukkur, Ingrian kukkoro, Karelian kukkaro, Veps kukor), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kukur (compare German Köcher, Old English cocer), although there is no consensus about reconstructing this word to Proto-Germanic. This
From Proto-Finnic *kukkoi, derived from a borrowing from Proto-Germanic *kukkaz (“cock, rooster”).
From Proto-Finnic *kulta, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gulþą (compare Swedish guld, German Gold, English gold). Compare Livvi kultasen. Distant doublet of kelta.
From Proto-Finnic *kuningas (compare Estonian kuningas), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kuningaz (compare Icelandic konungur).

parole.significato: honor, honour (respect, favorable reputation; dignity; sense of self-worth)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kunnija (compare Ingrian kunnia, Karelian kunnivo, Votic kunnia), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kunją (compare Old Norse kyn, English kin). The meaning shifted from “family, clan” to “noble family, family honor” and finally to “honor”, perhaps by influence from Swedish ära, heder,

parole.significato: hoe (agricultural tool consisting of a long handle with a flat blade fixed perpendicular to it at the end)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kookka, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hōkaz. Cognate with Karelian kuokku and Veps kokš, as well as possibly koukku.
From Proto-Finnic *kuuro (compare Karelian kuuro- in kuuropeä, Veps kuro, Votic kuuro), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skūrō (“storm, rain shower”) (compare Swedish skur, English shower).

parole.significato: picture, figure (representation of visible reality produced by e.g. drawing)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kuva, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skuwwô (“shadow, reflection”) (whence Swedish skugga (“shadow”), Gothic 𐍃𐌺𐌿𐌲𐌲𐍅𐌰 (skuggwa, “mirror”)).
From Proto-Finnic *kubas, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kūbaz (whence Icelandic kúfur, Old Norse *kúfr (“elevation, heap, bulge, round top”)).

parole.significato: loin (part of the body between the ribs and hips)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kubëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hupiz.

parole.significato: squat, crouch (position assumed by bending deeply at the knees while resting on one's feet)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kükkü. Possibly ultimately sound-symbolic, but may also be a loan from Proto-Germanic *hukkōną or *hūkaną (compare Old Norse húka). Cognate with Estonian kükk, Karelian kyykkä, Livonian kikkõ and Veps kükta.
Possibly from Proto-Finnic *kügäs ~ *kük'äs, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skukkaz (compare Old Saxon skok). No cognates in other Finnic languages are known.
From Proto-Finnic *kärcidäk, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hardijaną (“to harden, endure”).

parole.significato: a wooden rack with many branches used to dry grain
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kärbäs ~ *kärbis, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *harbaz.

parole.significato: to visit, go to (and return), attend (a place)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *käüdäk (“to walk; to ferment”) (compare Karelian käyvvä, Estonian käima), from earlier *käwe-, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skēwijaną (compare Gothic 𐍃𐌺𐌴𐍅𐌾𐌰𐌽 (skēwjan), Old Norse skæva).

parole.significato: poor (with few or no possessions or money)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *keühä, likely borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skeuhaz (“shy”).
From Proto-Finnic *lagës, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *slagiz. Doublet of laji.

parole.significato: rotten (of wood or a similar solid material: overridden with bacteria, thus decayed and no longer able to e.g. support…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *laho, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (“fallen tree”), compare Old Norse lág (“lying tree”). Doublet of lieka and lieko
From Proto-Finnic *laihvo (compare Estonian lõiv, dialectal Finnish laihvo, Ingrian laiho, Karelian laiho, Votic laivo), borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Icelandic leiga).
From Proto-Finnic *laikka (compare Estonian laik), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *blaikaz (“pale, white”).
From Proto-Finnic *laihna, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *laihną (compare Swedish lån, English loan).
From Proto-Finnic *lainëh, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hlainiz (“leaning”).

From Proto-Finnic *laupijo, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *laubijǭ (compare Proto-West Germanic *laubijā). The word also has the dialectal variant laupio; the -ai- ~ -au- variation remains unexplained.

parole.significato: edge, margin, border, verge, brink, side (outer limit, or the area right beside the outer limit, of something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *laita (“edge, border”) (compare Estonian laid, Ingrian laita, Karelian laita, Veps laid, Votic laitõ). Probably related to *laita (“route, way”) (which could rather be the direct origin of the sense "state of affairs"), in which case borrowed from Proto-Germanic *laidō.
From Proto-Finnic *lagittadak (“to place”), borrowed and derived from Proto-Germanic *lagjaną (“to lay”).
From Proto-Finnic *lagittadak (“to criticize”), borrowed and derived from Proto-Germanic *lahaną (“to blame”), or of the same origin as laittaa (etymology 1).
From Proto-Finnic *laiva, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *flawją; cognates include Estonian laev. Compare also Lithuanian lai̇̃vas (“ship”).
From Proto-Finnic *lakëda (compare Ingrian lakkia, Ludian laged, Votic lakka), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *flakaz and nativized with *-ëda.

parole.significato: summit (topmost point of e.g. a hill or trajectory)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *laki (compare Estonian lagi), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *flakô (compare Old Norse flaki).
From Proto-Finnic *lakka, probably at least partially from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Norse flaki (“wicker fence or barrier”)).

parole.significato: lodging (condition of a plant that has been flattened in the field)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lako (compare Estonian lagu, Ingrian lako), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *lagą (compare Old Norse lag (“stratum, layer”)).

parole.significato: sheep (woolly ruminant of the genus Ovis; either used generically or referring more specifically to a female mature one)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lambas (compare Estonian lammas), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *lambaz (“lamb”) (compare Swedish lamm, English lamb).

parole.significato: thread (twisted strand of fiber used in sewing, weaving or in the construction of string)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lanka (compare Livonian lānga, Veps lang), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *langô.

parole.significato: brother-in-law (brother of one's spouse; husband of one's sibling)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lanko, borrowed from an unknown derivation of Proto-Germanic *langōną (whence Old English ġelangian, Old High German gilangōn). The original meaning was simply "relative", shifting into "relative by marriage, in-law" and finally "brother-in-law".
From Proto-Finnic *landëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *landį̄ (“loin”). Cognates include Veps landeh, Ludian landeh, Karelian lanneh.

parole.significato: to stack, pile up, line up
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *latoidak (compare Estonian laduma, Votic lattoa), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hlaþaną (compare Icelandic hlaða (“to pile, to stack”)).

parole.significato: onion (any plant of the genus Allium); (in the plural) the genus Allium
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *laukka (compare Estonian lauk, Livonian lōka), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *laukaz (“leek”) (compare Swedish lök, German Lauch, English leek).
From Proto-Finnic *lauma, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *flaumaz. No cognates in other Finnic languages are known (other than a marginal Livvi borrowing from Finnish).
From Proto-Finnic *lausas (“loose”), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *lausaz.
From Proto-Finnic *lautta (compare Karelian lautta, Veps laut), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *flautaz (“float, stream”).

parole.significato: to cut (divide with a sharp instrument)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lëik'at'ak (compare Estonian lõikama (“to cut”)), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *blaikijaną; see the Proto-Finnic entry for more details.

From Proto-Finnic *laipa (compare Estonian leib (“bread”)), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hlaibaz (compare German Laib (“loaf”), English loaf, Gothic 𐌷𐌻𐌰𐌹𐍆𐍃 (hlaifs, “bread”)). Slavic words like Russian хлеб (xleb, “bread”) are likewise borrowed from Germanic.
From Proto-Finnic *lëivo, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *laiwaz (whence *laiwazikǭ). Related to Estonian lõo.

parole.significato: to dehusk (to remove the husk from)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lestäk (Karelian lessä is an exact cognate; also compare Ingrian lesemet, Votic lesemed and dialectal Estonian lesemed), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *lesaną.
The adessive of the stem levä- with a possessive suffix, from Proto-Finnic *levä- (compare Karelian levälläh, Votic levällä), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *lewō (compare Old Norse ljá).
From Proto-Finnic *lebäit'äk (compare Estonian lebama, Veps lebeita, Votic leväte), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *slēpaną.

parole.significato: tether (rope, cable etc. that holds something in place whilst allowing some movement)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lëëka, borrowed from early Proto-Germanic *lēgā (later Proto-Germanic *lēgō). Compare Middle Dutch lage (“trap, snare”). Doublet of laho and lieko

parole.significato: fallen, rotten tree, especially one that is in water
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lëëko, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *lēgō. Doublet of laho and lieka.
From Proto-Finnic *leevä, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hlēwaz.

parole.significato: cloth (piece of garment used on furniture, for cleaning, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *liina (compare Karelian liina, Veps lin), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *līną (“flax”) (compare English linen, German Lein, Swedish lin). Related also to Estonian lina (“flax, linen”), which was borrowed separately from Slavic or Baltic.

Formally, an -e-derivative from a causative in -ttaa, though no verb *liivattaa is attested. The root is the now-obsolete liiva (“slime”), from Proto-Finnic *liiva, ultimately a loan from Proto-Germanic *slīwą (whence also e.g. Icelandic slý). First attested in 1896.

parole.significato: dirt, filth, stain, muck (foreign substance that makes something unclean)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lika, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *slīką. Related to Estonian liga, Ingrian lika, Karelian lika /liga and Ludian lʹiga.
From Proto-Finnic *lima, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *slīmą.

parole.significato: to shine, glow, glare, sparkle (to emit light)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *loistadak, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *glōaną, *glōjaną, and derived further with + -istaa. Related to Veps loštta and dialectal Estonian loistuda.
From Proto-Finnic *lunas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *lunaz (“ransom”). The reason for the geminated -nn- is not clear.

From Proto-Finnic *loodëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *flōduz (compare German Flut, Swedish flod) and derived with + -e. Originally meant flood or high tide; the sense "ebb" is a literary invention from the 1830s. See also vuoksi for further details.

parole.significato: hay that is cut/mown and left on the ground to dry
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *looko, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?], whence Icelandic slægja and dialectal Swedish slog.
From Proto-Finnic *lustëh, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *luhstǭ.
From Proto-Finnic *makjas. borrowed from Proto-Germanic *smakjaz.

From Proto-Finnic *mahti (compare Estonian maht, Veps maht), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *mahtiz (whence also Old Swedish makt, Swedish makt). A more recent borrowing from Swedish has also been proposed. Probably also influenced by mahtaa. The adjective sense is probably by re-extraction from words
From Proto-Finnic *mainit'ak, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *mainijaną. Doublet of meinata.

parole.significato: synonym of muikku (“vendace”), especially vendace living in or fished from the Bothnian Bay
parole.testo: Variant of maima, from Proto-Finnic *maima, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *maiwaz. Also related to Northern Sami máivi.
From Proto-Finnic *mako, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *magô.
From Proto-Finnic *maldas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *maltaz (“malt”), variant of *maltą.

parole.significato: flesh (soft, often edible, parts of fruits, vegetables, mushrooms)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *malto, possibly a conflation of two unrelated Germanic roots, Proto-Germanic *maltaz (“soft”) and Proto-Germanic *smultą (“molten fat, lard”).
From Proto-Finnic *manat'ak, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *manōną.
From Proto-Finnic *marhaminta, a compound derived from two Germanic borrowings, Proto-Germanic *marhaz (“horse”) + Proto-Germanic *minþla (“bridle”).

parole.significato: bedstraw (any plant of the genus Galium)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *matara, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *madarǭ.
From Proto-Finnic [Term?], borrowed from Proto-Germanic *mauraz. Cognate with Karelian mauroi, Livvi mauroi, and Ludian mauroi.

parole.significato: a leprechaun-like creature that is friendly to humans and prefers darkness
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mendinkä(inen), borrowed from early Proto-Germanic *menþingō (later *minþingō), compare Icelandic minning (“memory (of the deceased)”).

parole.significato: pot, cage trap (a trap for fishing crabs, fish, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mërta, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Swedish mjärde (“pot, trap”)).
From Proto-Finnic *mëëkka (compare Estonian mõõk), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *mēkijaz or its Gothic descendant (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).
From Proto-Finnic *mees (compare Estonian mees, Livonian mīez), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *mēgaz (compare Gothic 𐌼𐌴𐌲𐍃 (mēgs)).

parole.significato: mold, mull (humus); soil or earth suitable for growing plants, a mixture of mineral soil and humus
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *multa, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *muldō (earlier *muldā), compare Gothic 𐌼𐌿𐌻𐌳𐌰 (mulda, “dust”) and English mould. Cognates include Estonian muld, Votic multõ, Ingrian multa, Livonian mūlda.

parole.significato: shape, form, figure (physical appearance or outline)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mooto, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *mōtą. Doublet with muotti.
From Proto-Finnic *murkina, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *murginaz (“morning”). The meaning has shifted from "breakfast" to "food".

parole.significato: scratch, scrape (disruption or mark on a surface)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic [Term?] (compare Estonian narmas, Livonian nārmaz), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *narwô (“scar”) (compare German Narbe (“scar”)).

parole.significato: beard moss, beard lichen, old man's beard (several genera of lichen that grow hanging from trees)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *naava, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?].

parole.significato: leather (tough material produced from the skin of animals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nahka (compare Estonian nahk), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *naskiz, *naskaz (“soft leather”) (compare Old English næsc (“soft leather; deer skin”)).

parole.significato: nail (spike-shaped fastener, now often made of metal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nakla (compare Estonian nael), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *naglaz (compare Swedish nagel). * ((coat) peg): The first coat pegs were often simply nails hammered on a wall and left to protrude out. * (unit of weight): Perhaps a later semantic loan from Germanic; in some varieties
From Proto-Finnic *nauttidak (“to use, enjoy”), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *nautijaną (“to use, employ”).

From Proto-Finnic *nëkla (compare Estonian nõel, Ingrian neegla, Karelian niekla /niegla, Votic niglõ), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *nēþlō (compare Gothic 𐌽𐌴𐌸𐌻𐌰 (nēþla), Swedish nål, English needle).

parole.significato: to mow, mow down, cut, cut down, scythe, reap (crops, hay, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *niittädäk, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *snīþaną and further derived with *-tadak, thus equivalent to niit- + -tää.
From Proto-Finnic *nootta, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *nōtō. Cognate with Estonian noot, Ingrian nootta, Karelian nuotta, Livvi nuottu, Ludian nuot, Veps not, Võro nuut and Votic noottõ.

From Proto-Finnic [Term?] (compare Estonian näsi- in näsiniin), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *natją (compare Gothic 𐌽𐌰𐍄𐌹 (nati)). The semantic development would be "net" > "bast" (which was used to make nets) > "mezereon".

parole.significato: rein (strap or rope attached to the bridle or bit, used to control a horse or other animal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ohja (compare Estonian ohi), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *ansijō (compare Old Norse æs).
From Proto-Finnic *oncca, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *anþiją.
From Proto-Finnic *padëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *paþaz.
From Proto-Finnic *paikka (compare Estonian paik and Votic paikkõ), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *spaikǭ (compare English spoke).
From Proto-Finnic *paistadak, probably borrowed from Northwest Germanic *bājan-, from Proto-Germanic *bēaną.
From Proto-Finnic *paita (compare Karelian paita, Veps paid), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *paidō (compare Old High German pheit and Gothic 𐍀𐌰𐌹𐌳𐌰 (paida)).

parole.significato: bellows (device for delivering pressurized air in a controlled quantity to a controlled location)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *palgëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *balgiz (“bag”). Related to Ludian palgiž.

parole.significato: a type of horse cart traditionally used to transport barrels of tar
parole.testo: Possibly from Proto-Finnic [Term?], borrowed from Proto-Germanic *balkuz.

parole.significato: hardpan (especially one in the bottom of a body of water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *palci, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *falþį̄, *falþaz.
From Proto-Finnic *panta, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *bandą. Compare English band, Estonian pand.

parole.significato: A unit of volume for firewood, enough firewood to make a woodpile four kyynärä (around 2.4 metres) long and three kyynä…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *parmas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *barmaz.
From Proto-Finnic *pardas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *bardaz (“edge”), compare Old Norse barð (“brim, verge”). Cognates include Estonian parras, Livonian pārdaz, Ludian pardaz.

parole.significato: mattress (a pad on which a person can recline and sleep)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *patja (compare Estonian padi), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *badją (compare German Bett). Doublet of peti.

parole.significato: sting (bump on skin after having been stung)
parole.testo: According to LÄGLOS, from Proto-Finnic *pauka, which is borrowed from Proto-Germanic *baugaz (“bend”). Probably further derived with + -ma.
From Proto-Finnic *pakla (compare Estonian pael, Ingrian pagla, Livvi paglu, Veps pagl, Votic paglõ), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *fatilaz (compare German Fessel).
From Proto-Finnic *peittädäk, possibly derived from a borrowing of Proto-Germanic *bē(j)aną. Related to Estonian peitma, Ingrian peittää, Ludian peitada, Veps peittädä and Votic peittää (Kattila).

parole.significato: field (wide, open space used to grow crops)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pëlto (compare Estonian põld, Veps pöud, Votic põlto), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *felþą (compare English field).
From Proto-Finnic *përgat'ak, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *berganą (“to take care of, to keep”), in which case, a doublet with pärjätä. This has been disputed however.

parole.significato: cleat (strip of wood fastened on transversely to something in order to give strength, prevent warping, hold position, e…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pëëna, perhaps borrowed from Proto-Germanic *spēnuz (“piece of wood”).

From Proto-Finnic *pika (compare Estonian pea, Karelian pika, Livonian pigā, Veps piga, Votic pigaa), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *fiką (compare Danish fige, Swedish fika (“to strive (for)”)).

parole.significato: jeer, mockery, mock, ridicule, jest, derision
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pilkka, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *blikkaz (compare German Blick).
From Proto-Finnic *pino, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *fīnō (“heap”).

parole.significato: surface (top side of something; outer hull of a tangible object)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pinta (compare Estonian pind), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *spindaz (compare Old English spind, Dutch spint (spinthout)).
From Proto-Finnic *pordas, borrowed from Northwest Germanic *bordaz, from earlier Proto-Germanic *burdą. Cognate with Karelian porras, Veps pordaz. Doublet of pursi.
From Proto-Finnic *punta (“old unit of weight”) (compare Estonian pund, Livonian pūnda), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *pundą (“pound, weight”), itself from Latin pondō.
From Proto-Finnic *purha, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *fursaz.
From Proto-Finnic *purilas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *burilaz (whence Norwegian byrel, byrdel). No cognates in other Finnic languages are known.
From Proto-Finnic *purci, from earlier *purti, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *burdą.

parole.significato: to strive, endeavour, seek to, pursue [with illative or allative; or (with verbs) with illative of third infinitive] (t…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pürkidäk, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wurkijaną.

From Proto-Finnic *pühkidäk (compare Estonian pühkima, Ingrian pyyhkiä, Karelian pyyhkie, Ludian pühkida, Veps pühkta, Votic pühčiä), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wiskijaną (compare German wischen, Dutch wissen).

parole.significato: hem (border of an article of clothing doubled back and stitched together)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pärmeh, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *barmiz (compare Old Norse barmr (“rim”)).

parole.significato: table, desk (standing piece of furniture with a flat top)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *peütä, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *beudaz (compare Old English bēod, Gothic 𐌱𐌹𐌿𐌸𐍃 (biuþs)).
From Proto-Finnic *raaka (compare Estonian raag- in Estonian raagnahk), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hrawaz.

parole.significato: yard (horizontal spar on the mast of a sailing ship)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raaka (compare Estonian raag), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rahō (compare German Rah, Rahe (“yard”), Swedish rå (“yard”)).

parole.significato: robust, strong (especially of an adult man or adult male animal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raavas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þrawwaz (“full-grown”). Doublet of rahvas (“riff raff, peasantry”).

parole.significato: money (means of exchange and measure of value)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raha, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skrahā (“squirrel skin”) (later Proto-Germanic *skrahō; compare Old Norse skrá). Originally, this word referred to animal furs (especially squirrel pelts), since they were a common payment instrument before notes and coins were introduced. Attes

parole.significato: trace, tug (strap used to join the shafts of a carriage, sled etc. or a shaft bow to the horse collar)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rahkëh, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *dragiz, from *draganą.

parole.significato: quark, tvorog (soft creamy curd cheese made by souring or fermenting milk and removing the whey from it)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rahka, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *dragjō (“dregs”).

parole.significato: the common people, the lower orders (historically, the common people as opposed to the gentry); rabble, riffraff, vulgu…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rahvas (compare Estonian rahvas (“people”)), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þrawwaz (“full-grown”), in which case a variant of raavas, which has remained closer to the original meaning. Compare the sense development in väki.
From Proto-Finnic *raippa, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *raipaz (“cord, rope”).
From Proto-Finnic *raita, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *spraiþō (compare Old High German spreid, spreida (“bush”)).

parole.significato: to clear (remove obstructions, impediments or unwanted items from)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raivat'ak, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *strawjaną (“to strew”).
From Proto-Finnic *rak'as (compare Karelian rakas (“willing, eager, kind, dear”)), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *frakaz (“greedy, lustful”).

parole.significato: dregs, draff (settled sediment of alcoholic fermented drinks, such as beer)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rapa (“dregs”), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *drabaz. Cognates include Estonian raba, Karelian rapa, Livonian rabād, Veps raba and Votic rapa.

parole.significato: box, case, container, casket, carton (mostly one of relatively small size)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *racja (compare dialectal Estonian rasi), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *randjaz (compare Swedish rände).
From Proto-Finnic *rasva, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).

From Proto-Finnic *rata (compare Estonian rada, Ingrian rata (“The Milky Way”), Karelian rata (“The Milky Way”), Livonian radā), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *tradō (compare Dutch tra (“trail, (forest) path”)).
Adessive plural of ratsas, from Proto-Finnic *rac'as, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *raidijaz, *raidaz (whence Old English ræde (“ready to ride, mounted (on a horse)”).

parole.significato: gland (organ that synthesizes and secretes substance)
parole.testo: rauha + -nen, diminutive of a dialectal word that is from Proto-Finnic *rauha (“gland, swelling”) (compare Estonian rahu, Ingrian rauha, Karelian rauhna, Livonian ro’ugõz, Votic ravvu), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Norse hrœrar (“groin”)).

parole.significato: to work hard; to toil, to drudge
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rehkidäk (earlier *reški-), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þreskaną.

parole.significato: span, distance between posts on a fence (now especially a roundpole fence), hayrack, etc.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rëhto, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wrehtuz.
From Proto-Finnic *rëngas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hrengaz (> *hringaz) (“ring”). Doublet of rinki.

From Proto-Finnic *rëëhudak (related to Karelian riehuo and Veps rehuda). Further origin is disputed; theories include relation to riesa, borrowing from Proto-Germanic *rēsōną (compare Middle Dutch rasen), or an original sound-symbolic root.

parole.significato: to tear, rip, rend (by pulling with hands, especially something off from plants, like fruit)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *riipidäk, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rīfaną.

parole.significato: argument, dispute, disagreement, quarrel, verbal fight, contest
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *riita (compare Estonian riid, Livvi riidu, Ludian riid, Veps rida), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *strīdaz (compare German Streit, Icelandic stríð).

From Proto-Finnic *riittädäk. Related to Ingrian riittää and Karelian riitteä. The original meaning was "to cover with (thin) ice" (whence riite), from which "to cover" and abstractly "to suffice". If from earlier *riip-tä- (with *-tä-), the root could be a borrowing from Proto-Germanic *hrīmô (geni
From Proto-Finnic *rik'as (compare Estonian rikas), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rīkaz, *rīkijaz (compare Swedish rik (“rich”)).
From Proto-Finnic *ripsi, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hrispō. Related to Estonian ripse, Karelian ripsi, Ludian ripš, Veps rips and Votic ripsi.

parole.significato: pole (delimbed and usually not debarked stem of a small tree, especially one cut to a specified length for a purpose)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *riuku (compare Ingrian riuku, Karelian riuku, Votic riuku and dialectal Estonian riug), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Norse þrjúgr).
From Proto-Finnic *roukka, *roukko, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hraukaz. Cognates include Estonian rõuk, Veps rouk, Ingrian roukko.

parole.significato: carcass, dead body, especially of a slaughtered animal
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ruho, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?], cognate with Old Norse hrør (“corpse, scrap, wreck, debris”).

parole.significato: prince (ruler or head of a principality; male member of a royal family)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ruhtinas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *druhtinaz.
From Proto-Finnic *rugis (compare Estonian rukis, Veps rugiž), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rugiz (compare Old English ryġe).
From Proto-Finnic *rukka, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rukkaz. Doublet of frakki and rukki.

parole.significato: grass (mass noun); blade of grass (individual specimen)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rooho, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *grōsō- (“grass”).

parole.significato: food (any substance consumed by living organisms to sustain life)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rooka (compare Estonian roog, Ludian ruog, Votic rookõ), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rōkā (“care, attention”) (compare Middle High German ruoche, Middle Low German rōke). Compare ruokkia.
From Proto-Finnic *rookkidak, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rōkijaną, whence Old English rēcan. Compare with ruoka.
From Proto-Finnic *rookko, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rōkō (“care, attention”). Doublet of ruoka.
From Proto-Finnic *rooma, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (whence Old Norse drómi).
From Proto-Finnic *roostëk, derived from a borrowing from Proto-Germanic *rustaz. Cognates include Estonian rooste, Swedish rost, English rust.
From Proto-Finnic *rooto, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rōdō (“rod, pole”). Cognate to Veps rod.
From Proto-Finnic *rupi (compare Veps rubi, Votic rupi), borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Norse hrufa (“scab”)).

parole.significato: dugout (boat made from a hollowed-out log)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ruuhi, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þrūhs (“excavated trunk, trough”). Cognates include Estonian ruhi, Karelian ruuhi, Ingrian ruuhi.

parole.significato: congestion, lots of traffic, traffic jam
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ruhka, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hrūgǭ (compare modern Swedish råge (“more than full measure”)), perhaps originally meaning "heap".

parole.significato: cluster (bunch or group of several discrete items that are close to each other)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rübäs (compare Karelian rypäs), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (whence Proto-West Germanic *þrūbō).

parole.significato: mucus, snot (viscous mucus from the nose)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *räkä, an early borrowing from Proto-Germanic *hrēką. Cognates include Estonian röga, Old English hrāca, Old Norse hráki.
From Proto-Finnic *räüstäs (compare Estonian räästas, Veps räustaz), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hraustaz (compare Old Norse raust, Swedish röste (“roof truss”)).

From Proto-Finnic *saip(p)u-, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *saipǭ (“soap”) (compare Swedish såpa) or later Proto-Norse [script needed] (*saipwōn-). The variant saipua is attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552) and modern saippua first in 1609. Doublet of suopa and soopa. The
From Proto-Finnic *sairas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sairaz, compare Swedish sår, English sore.
From Proto-Finnic *sakko, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sakō.
From Proto-Finnic *salaga (compare dialectal salaja, no other Finnic cognates are known), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *salhô (“willow”) (compare Swedish sälg, English sallow).
From Proto-Finnic *sallidak (compare Estonian sallima, Karelian sallie), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *saljaną (compare Swedish sälja, English sell).

parole.significato: bolt, bar (bar to prevent a door from being forced open; sliding pin or bar in a lock)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *salpa (compare Karelian salpa, Veps saub), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *stalpą (whence dialectal Swedish stalpe (“pole”)).

From Proto-Finnic *sama (compare Estonian sama, Karelian sama, Votic sama), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *samaz (compare Swedish samma, English same; also borrowed into Sami, compare Northern Sami seamma).

parole.significato: (either of) a pair of sticks used to carry hay
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sapilas, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *stapulaz.

parole.significato: sedge (any plant of the genus Carex)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sara (compare Karelian sara, Ludian sara, Veps šarahin), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *staraz (compare Swedish starr).

parole.significato: harbour/harbor, port, haven (place where ships can shelter or dock for loading or unloading)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *satama (cognate with Estonian sadam (“harbour”)). Two etymologies exist: * Derivation from sataa in the sense "to descend". * Derivation with the suffix + -ma from a root derived from Proto-Germanic *staþaz (compare English stathe, German Gestade).
From Proto-Finnic *satula, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sadulaz (“saddle”). Cognate with Estonian sadul.

From Proto-Finnic *sakna (compare southeastern dialectal saakna, sakna, Estonian saun), possibly borrowed from early Proto-Germanic *stakna- (later *stakkaz, whence English stack). Older sense "winter dwelling, a pit dug into snow for temporary shelter", compare Northern Sami suovdnji (“pit dug in s
From Proto-Finnic *sapra, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *stauraz. Cognate with Karelian soapra, Livvi suabru, Ludian suabr and Veps sabr.
From Proto-Finnic *sëkla (compare Estonian sõel, Karelian šiekla, Ingrian seegla, Votic siglõ), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sēdlą (compare Swedish såll, Icelandic sáld).
From Proto-Finnic *siima, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sīmô. Cognate with dialectal Estonian sihm, Ingrian siima, Karelian siima, Livvi siimu, Ludian šiim, Veps siim, sim and Votic siimõ.
From Proto-Finnic *siivilä, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sīhwila, *sīhila (“sieve”).

parole.significato: place, stead (location or position of or for something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sija (compare Ludian šija), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *stiją (compare English sty in pigsty and Swedish stia in svinstia). First adapted to mean “(grammatical) case” by Finnish physician and philologist Elias Lönnrot in 1836.

parole.significato: a nonalcoholic or low-alcohol drink made from lemon, various sugars and water, common around vappu (“May Day”)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sima, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *saimaz (compare German Seim (“syrup”), Old Norse seimr (“honeycomb”)). The original meaning was “mead”, but the common meaning now refers to a different beverage, albeit one that is ultimately developed from mead.

parole.significato: herd of horses, sheep or reindeers
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *soota, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *stōdą.
From Proto-Finnic *surku, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *surgō (compare English sorrow, Swedish sorg).
From Proto-Finnic *tadëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *tadą (compare Old Norse tað, Icelandic tað, dialectal Swedish tad), further derived + -e.

parole.significato: magic (use of supernatural rituals, forces etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *taika, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *taikną.

parole.significato: dough, pastry (mix of flour and other ingredients)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *taikina, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?], from *daigaz (“dough”).

parole.significato: a large fish-trap made of wire or sticks, meant to be placed in a flowing body of water with the mouth facing upstream
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tainijo, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *tainijǭ.
From Proto-Finnic *tappo, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?].
From Proto-Finnic *tarit'ak, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *tarjaną. Related to Karelian tarita, Ludian tarita and Veps tarita.
From Proto-Finnic *tarbis, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þarbaz, *þarbiz, *þarbijaz (“needed, useful”). Cognate with Ingrian tarvis, Estonian tarvis.
From Proto-Finnic *tauko, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *taugō.

parole.significato: one of the logs or other (round) pieces of wood placed under something, such as a boat or a pile of firewood, to keep i…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tëla (compare Ingrian tela, Karelian tela, Veps tela), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þelą. Doublet of teli.
From Proto-Finnic *tëljo, borrowed from early Proto-Germanic *þeljǭ (later Proto-Germanic *þiljǭ). Compare Karelian tel’l’o.

parole.significato: bolt (bar to prevent a door from being forced open; sliding pin or bar in a lock)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *telki, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *telgô.

parole.significato: An animal to be slaughtered; an animal for slaughter.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tëpras (compare Estonian tõbras), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þeuraz (“bull”), from Proto-Indo-European *táwros; originally meant "bull". Doublet of Taurus, tarvas, and torvi.
From Proto-Finnic *tina, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *tiną (“tin”).
From Proto-Finnic *tiuhta (whence also Estonian tihv), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *stiftaz (whence German Stift).
From Proto-Finnic *tuhka, likely borrowed from Proto-Germanic *tuska-, *tuskijaną (“to torch, to burn”). Cognate of Estonian tuhk.
From Proto-Finnic *tunkijo, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *dungijǭ.

parole.significato: to sentence, condemn (declare a sentence on a convicted person)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *toomit'ak, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *dōmijaną (“to judge”), compare Swedish döma (“to sentence, to judge”) and Old High German tuomen (“to judge”).
From Proto-Finnic *tuppi (compare Estonian tupp), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *duppaz (“hollow”).
From Proto-Finnic *turska (compare Estonian tursk), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þurskaz (“cod”).

parole.significato: protection, safety, security (condition or feeling of being safe)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *turva (compare Estonian turv, Ingrian turva, Karelian turva, Livvi turvu, Veps turvane and Votic turvõ), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *trūwō (compare Swedish tro).

parole.significato: peat, turf (soil formed of dead but not fully decayed plants found in bog areas)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *turbëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *turbz, whence also English turf. Finnic cognates include Estonian turvas, Ingrian turve, Karelian turveh, Livonian dūrbal, Livvi turveh, Ludian turbiž, turbeh, Veps turbiž, turbaz, turbez, Võro turbas and Votic turvaz (Kattila).
From Proto-Finnic *tiüris (compare Finnish dialectal tiyris), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *diurijaz.

parole.significato: bank, embankment (relatively small edge of a river or another body of water)
parole.testo: Possibly from Proto-Finnic *teüräs (no cognates), if borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old English þéor (“swelling, protuberance”)).

From Proto-Finnic *umpi, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *umbi (“around, about, by, near”), which was perhaps already borrowed into Proto-Finno-Saamic (compare Northern Sami oppa (“whole; quite a”)).
From Proto-Finnic *upëda, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare German üppig). No cognates in other Finnic languages are known.

parole.significato: to believe, have faith [with illative ‘in’] (someone's abilities, chances etc.; someone's existence; the power, value e…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *uskodak, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wunskijaną.

parole.significato: haze, mist (very fine particles of water vapor in the air slightly limiting visibility)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *utu (compare Estonian udu), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Icelandic úði (“drizzle”)).

vai(k)- + -eta, from Proto-Finnic *vaikka (“quiet”), probably a borrowing from Proto-Germanic *waikwaz. Cognate with Ingrian vaiketa as well as adjectival Estonian vaikne, Livvi vaikkaine and adverbial Veps vaikńe.
From Proto-Finnic *vainaga, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wainagaz, see it for more.

parole.significato: diaper (US), nappy (UK), napkin (South Africa) (absorbent garment worn by a baby, or by someone who is incontinent)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vaippa (compare Estonian vaip, Votic vaippa (Kattila)), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *waipaz (compare Old Norse veipa (“a kind of piece of clothing”), Gothic 𐍅𐌰𐌹𐍀𐍃 (waips, “crown, wreath”)).
From Proto-Finnic *vaiva, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *waiwō (“woe, misery, pain”).
From Proto-Finnic *valit'ak (compare Estonian valima, Karelian valita, Veps valita, Võro valima, valitsõma, Votic valittsa), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *waljaną and further derived with + -ita.
From Proto-Finnic *valdit'ak, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *waldaną and further derived with + -ita.

From Proto-Finnic *valta, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *waldą (“might, power, authority”) or Proto-Norse [script needed] (*walda-) (compare Swedish våld, German Gewalt, Dutch geweld, Icelandic vald). First attested in 1215 (in the surname Kaikewalde).
From Proto-Finnic *vatnas (compare Estonian vannas, Livonian va’dmõl (“stem of a ship”), Ludian vannaz, Veps vadnaz), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wagnaz.

parole.significato: hoop, band (of a barrel, or a similar ring used to bind an object)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vandëh, from earlier *vandeš, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wanduz. Cognate with Karelian vanneh, Veps vandeh, Ludian vandeh.
From Proto-Finnic *vant'us, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wantuz (“glove, mitten”).

parole.significato: reserve, backup (that which is reserved or kept back, as for future use)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vara (compare Estonian vara), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *warō (compare Swedish vara (“goods”), vara (“care”), English ware (“aware”), aware, ware (“goods”)).
From Proto-Finnic *vargas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wargaz.
From Proto-Finnic *varp'ëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] *hwerbaną "to turn", (whence Swedish varv (“layer, turn, layer of logs in building”)). Doublet of varvi.

parole.significato: guard, security guard (a person employed to provide security for specific people or specific property)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vartija, *vartja, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?]. Related to Estonian vardja (“bailiff”), Karelian vartie.
From Proto-Finnic *vartodak, equivalent to vart- + -oa, the root being borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wardāną.

parole.significato: a type of small seine (fishing net)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vata, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wadaz (compare Swedish vad, Old Norse vaðr).

parole.significato: small ring or loop made of wicker
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vakla, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wadlaz (whence English wattle).

From Proto-Finnic *vapras (compare Estonian vapper, Karelian vabras, Võro vabras), probably originally meaning "lively, brisk, breezy, healthy", possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wabraz (no exact Germanic descendants are known, but it would be from the same root that gave Old Norse vafra).
From Proto-Finnic *velji (compare Estonian veli and further also Northern Sami viellja), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *swelijô (compare Old Norse svilar).
From Proto-Finnic *venät (genitive *venäden), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *winidaz (“Slav”).

parole.significato: broadcloth; a dense but (relatively) thin, short-pile, fairly smooth-faced woolen fabric woven of carded yarn, either p…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vërka, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *werką (“rope, cord”).
From Proto-Finnic *verkilo, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wergilaz (whence Old Norse virgill).

parole.significato: match (equal or superior in comparison) (now mostly used in a number of idiomatic expressions)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vërta, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *werþaz (“worthy”). Doublet of väärti and vörtti.

parole.significato: wort (liquid extract from the ground malt and grain soaked in hot water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *verdek, borrowed from early Proto-Germanic *wertiz (later *wirtiz), and derived with + -e. Cognate with Estonian virre, Ingrian veerre, Livonian vīrdig and Votic virre.

parole.significato: In some traditional hunting traps, a fence that serves to guide the prey towards the trap.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vihi, probably a borrowing from Proto-Germanic *wīsijaną.
From Proto-Finnic *vihko (“bundle”), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wiskō, *wiskaz (“bundle of hay”).

parole.significato: liquor (US), spirits (UK, AU, NZ) (distilled alcoholic beverage; rather strong and often clear, such as vodka)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *viina, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wīną, from Latin vīnum. Doublet of viini.
From Proto-Finnic *viisas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wīsaz (compare Swedish vis (“wise”)).

parole.significato: A thicket of young deciduous trees.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *viita, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *widuz.
From Proto-Finnic *vika, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *swiką. Cognate with Estonian viga.

parole.significato: birch (stick, rod or bundle of twigs made from birch wood, used for punishment)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vicca, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wiþjǭ. Doublet of vitja.
From Proto-Finnic *viühti (compare Estonian viht, Karelian viyhti, Veps vihťak), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wiftiz (“weaving”).
From Proto-Finnic *väkä, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wēgǭ, *wēgō (whence German Waage and Swedish våg); see vaaka.

parole.significato: around (from one state or condition to an opposite or very different one)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ümpärik (compare Estonian ümber, Ingrian ympäär, Livonian immõr, Veps ümbri, Votic ümperi), equivalent to lative ympär- + -i, the root ultimately derived from Proto-Germanic *umbi.
From Proto-Finnic *äkedä. Equivalent to *äkä + -eä; the root is probably a front-vowel variant of *aka-, itself borrowed from Proto-Germanic *agaz. Related to Estonian äge and Karelian äkie.
